transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I just keep snapping at people lately. It's getting bad at work. Like the other day, we were in a safety meeting and I just... I started yelling before I could even stop myself. Now the younger inspectors on the floor act like they're scared to even ask me anything. I just need to figure out why my temper is so out of control.
Aside from this temper, have you been feeling persistently sad, empty, or lost interest in the things you usually enjoy over the past few weeks?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel sad or empty or anything like that. I still do the things I normally do when I get off my shift. It's just... it's really just the anger that's the problem. I haven't lost interest in my usual stuff, I just can't seem to keep my cool.
Do these outbursts seem to happen specifically when you are reminded of a past traumatic or life-threatening event?

Yeah, they do. It's... well, sometimes just a loud clank from a cart, or even just the smell of hot oil on the floor. It puts me right back in that bay. I just... I see my coworker right there by the machine like it's happening in front of me all over again. And if someone talks to me or asks for something right when that happens, I just completely lose my temper.
